summary: the cases of tests/run large under etude, against an ext2 read that takes a file's offset to 32 bits before it finds the block, an exFAT write that checks its offset against the format's limit and not its end, and a FAT32 write whose limit is 4 GiB and not 4 GiB less a byte

argv: sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: ext2-read-offset-32
faults.summary: ext2's read cuts a file's offset to 32 bits before it shifts it to a block, so that a read past 4 GiB reads the block 4 GiB below; the sparse row's mebibyte astride the 4 GiB line reads its upper half from the hole at the file's start

faults.name: exfat-limit-offset
faults.summary: exFAT's write checks its offset against the format's limit of 2^63 - 1 bytes and not the end of the write, so that a byte at the limit is let through and refused for space instead

lines: assert limit-named fail the kernel never says exfat:

faults.name: fat32-limit-4g
faults.summary: FAT32's write refuses only an offset past 4 GiB and not the end of the write, so that a byte at the last of 4 GiB, past the largest file of 4 GiB less a byte, is let through and refused for space instead

lines: assert limit-named fail the kernel never says vfat:
